title: CJP's Dipke Backs Jharkhand Students as JPSC Exam Scandal Triggers CID Probe
excerpt: Cockroach Janta Party founder extends solidarity to Jharkhand aspirants protesting alleged irregularities in state civil services and NET exams, as CID raids JPSC headquarters and suspends entire 2026 exam calendar.
body:
• CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has declared solidarity with Jharkhand students protesting alleged irregularities in the JPSC civil services exam and NET, saying the movement stands with students across all examinations.
  • Jharkhand's CID raided JPSC headquarters and detained eight individuals over allegations of OMR data manipulation and digital tampering in the 14th Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination.
  • The JPSC has suspended its entire 2026 exam calendar and deferred the Civil Services Main Examination indefinitely amid the investigation.
  • The development follows CJP's successful campaign that forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on July 25 and prompted the government to introduce exam reform legislation in parliament.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has extended his movement's support to students in Jharkhand who are protesting alleged irregularities in the state's public service commission examinations and the National Eligibility Test (NET). The move signals CJP's intent to broaden its campaign beyond the NEET paper leak controversy that forced Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation last week.

"CJP stands with all students. Whatever examinations are being compromised — whether NEET, CUET, SSC, NET, or state-level PSC exams — we will raise our voice until accountability is fixed."

— Abhijeet Dipke, CJP Founder

The JPSC Scandal Unfolds

The Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) is engulfed in a deepening crisis over alleged manipulation of results in the 14th Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination. A joint team of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and Ranchi Police conducted raids at eight locations, including the JPSC headquarters and the office of TSR Data Processing Private Limited (TSDPL), the agency contracted to conduct the exam, according to India News Stream.

Eight individuals were detained during the operation. Investigators seized computers, CPUs, laptops, hard disks, pen drives, server data, OMR scanning records, merit list documents, confidential files, and mobile phones. The CID is examining allegations of digital tampering, manipulation of OMR data, and irregularities in data transfer, with seized devices sent for forensic analysis.

The JPSC Controller of Examinations subsequently postponed the Combined Civil Services Main Examination-2025 and suspended all remaining exams under its 2026 calendar "until further orders." The decision has left thousands of aspirants in limbo.

A Blacklisted Agency at the Centre

A critical aspect of the investigation centres on how TSDPL was awarded the contract to conduct the 14th JPSC exam despite having been blacklisted by the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) in May 2025 over allegations of irregularities and confidentiality breaches. After the preliminary exam results were published, candidates flagged multiple red flags: results declared without cut-off marks, unsigned merit lists, unavailable OMR sheets, and a general lack of transparency in the process.

Workers of the BJP's Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) and state BJP leaders, including state president and Rajya Sabha MP Aditya Sahu, laid siege to the JPSC headquarters in Ranchi, demanding the cancellation of the preliminary exam. The protest led to confrontations between demonstrators and police.

CJP Extends Its Reach

Dipke's decision to back the Jharkhand students marks a significant expansion of the CJP's footprint beyond its original NEET-focused agitation. The movement, which began in May as a satirical online campaign after India's Chief Justice described unemployed youth as "cockroaches," grew into the biggest youth-led challenge Prime Minister Narendra Modi has faced since taking office in 2014, according to Reuters.

The CJP's education manifesto, released during its nationwide protest campaign, explicitly called for preventing paper leaks across all examinations, ensuring timely declaration of results, and strengthening accountability of examination authorities — demands that align squarely with the Jharkhand students' grievances.

CJP suspended its Jantar Mantar sit-in on July 26 after Pradhan resigned and the government agreed to address demands including compensation for families of students who died by suicide. Modi subsequently announced a task force headed by tech entrepreneur Nandan Nilekani to overhaul the country's exam system. On July 27, the government introduced a bill in parliament proposing tougher penalties for exam fraud, including longer prison terms and higher fines, according to Reuters.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For members of the Indian diaspora whose families remain tied to India's competitive exam ecosystem, the JPSC scandal underscores that the crisis of examination integrity extends well beyond national-level tests. State public service commissions, which control access to coveted government posts, face similar structural vulnerabilities. The CBI's filing of charges against 13 individuals over the NEET paper leak — including three NTA subject experts and coaching institute operatives — illustrates the scale of the problem.

What's Next

The CID investigation into the JPSC scandal is ongoing, with forensic examination of seized electronic devices expected to take several weeks. The Nilekani-led task force is yet to announce its terms of reference or timeline. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court has ordered no coercive action against student protesters and directed authorities to preserve all surveillance footage from the demonstrations, while ordering the release of detained minors, according to Reuters.

Dipke, who hinted at the Jantar Mantar camp that CJP was not going away, appears to be making good on that promise. "This is not the end," he said before leaving Delhi. "We will meet again soon."
